title: Al-Jami', the Gatherer
hook: the Gatherer, who will gather all
tomorrow: if God needs nothing, why does Dadi pray at all?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Muqsit, and a scale that not even anger is allowed to tip. The line: equitable. Today the whole week comes back, gathered in one place.

Saturday morning. Drop cloths, a borrowed ladder, a stack of paint cans by a tagged wall. Yesterday's question was who shows up. For Amira, the answer: her dad, Jordan, a thirteen-year-old in an old t-shirt, two neighbors nobody invited, and Dadi with a pot of food. People who'd never have stood in one place, standing in one place. That's today's Name in miniature. Al-Jami', the Gatherer.
screen: `SATURDAY. ONE WALL.` → `WHO SHOWS UP?` → `NEVER IN ONE PLACE, NOW IN ONE PLACE.`

segments.voice: Al-Jami', the Gatherer, who will gather all. The Qur'an speaks of a Day when Allah gathers all people together. And it speaks about gathering in this life, too, in a verse addressed to everyone: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another." Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: the verse doesn't say we were made different so we'd keep apart. It says so we'd come to know one another. Now the week, gathered on one wall. The Requiter: no wrong forgotten, so Amira never had to carry the payback herself. The Pardoner: erased, the way her dad wiped the grudge on the first morning. The Most Kind: tender, which turned out not to mean silent. Owner of all: a wall that was only ever on loan. Lord of Majesty and Generosity: a hot chocolate at the counter. The Equitable: a share a thirteen-year-old can carry, which today looks like a roller and a long wall. Six Names, and they all ended up standing on the same drop cloth.
screen: `HE WILL GATHER ALL.` · `NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.` · `THE WEEK ON ONE WALL.` · `SIX NAMES, ONE DROP CLOTH.` · then, large: `HE GATHERS.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the people who would come if you asked for help on a Saturday, one finger for each, and for every one of them a silent thank you. Then let one face stay with you: someone you haven't gathered with in a while. Hold them in mind until the bell.
screen: `ONE FINGER, ONE PERSON.` · `ONE FACE TO GATHER.`

segments.voice: Al-Jami'. The Gatherer, who brings together what's scattered, and who will gather all.
Keep this one: he gathers, the ones you'd invite and the ones you never would. A week of Names, gathered.

fork.setup: a new kid sits down at your lunch table and your friends go quiet. what does today's verse point you toward?
options: made different to know one another: ask them a real question.
people are happiest with their own group; let them find theirs.

fork.reveal: 49:13 doesn't erase the differences or wall them off. it gives them a purpose: that ye may know one another.
